stem:
Irfan uses last-digit and trailing-zero patterns to test whether a whole number can be a perfect cube.

Which claim is correct?

options.text: A perfect cube can end only in $0$, $1$, $4$, $5$, $6$, or $9$, as for perfect squares.
A whole number ending in exactly two zeros can be a perfect cube.
A perfect cube may end in any digit $0$ through $9$, and trailing zeros in a perfect cube come in groups of three.
Every whole number ending in $8$ is a perfect cube because $2^{3}=8$.

teacher.key_rationale: Cube units digits cover 0–9, unlike squares. Trailing zeros require factors in threes, so exactly two zeros is impossible. A copies square last-digit limits. B drops the groups-of-three rule. D over-reads the single case 2³=8.
